status.en: 154 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 22% fewer than the week before, most of them in Abuja, Lagos and Kaduna.
status.nb: 154 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 22 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Abuja, Lagos og Kaduna.

summary.en: Bandits in Zamfara continue to torch homes, burning families alive and abducting residents, while police in Ogun rescued ten abducted passengers and killed a suspected kidnapper in a gun battle. In Enugu gunmen attacked a compound, wounding five people. Cattle rustlers were repelled in Kaduna with the recovery of stolen cows. The conflict recorded 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Banditter i Zamfara fortsetter å brenne ned hus, brenne familier levende og bortføre innbyggere, mens politiet i Ogun reddet ti bortførte passasjerer og drepte en mistenkt kidnapper i en skyteskudd. I Enugu angrep bevæpnede menn et anlegg og såret fem personer. Kvegtyver ble avverget i Kaduna med tilbakelevering av stjålne kyr. Konflikten registrerte 1 486 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
